NGB1.claim: Tourists apply online for a Nagaland ILP: ₹200 per person for Indian tourists and ₹500 for foreign tourists, each valid 30 days. Tourists need no guarantor, only a local contact, and an application made in working hours may be approved within about four hours.

evidence.quote: Tourist (Domestic): Rs 200 per person valid for 30 days
Tourist(Foreigner): Rs 500 per person valid for 30 days
The ILP applicant falling in the category of tourists do not require a Guarantor.
if applied during working hours it may get approved within 4 (four) hours

NGB2.claim: Khonoma is about 20 km west of Kohima.

evidence.quote: Khonoma is a Western Angami Naga village located about 20 km west from Kohima

NGB3.claim: Dzükou is usually approached through Viswema and Jakhama, both within about 25 km of Kohima.

evidence.quote: The valley is most commonly approached from the Nagaland side through the Angami villages of Viswema and Jakhama (Zakhama), both within about 25 km (16 mi) of Kohima.

NGB4.claim: Kisama Heritage Village is 12 km from Kohima.

evidence.quote: Just 12 kms from Kohima, you can discover the Kisama Heritage Village

NGB10.claim: Kohima's nearest airport is Dimapur Airport and its nearest railway station is Dimapur.

evidence.quote: Nearest Airport : Dimapur Airport (DMU), Dimapur Nearest Railway Station : Dimapur Railway Station (DMV)

NGB11.claim: The whole of Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland is a Protected Area for foreign nationals, who need a Protected Area Permit.

evidence.quote: Whole of Manipur Whole of Mizoram Whole of Nagaland

NGB12.claim: Nagaland is known as the 'Land of Festivals'; its best-known festival, the Hornbill Festival, runs every year from 1 to 10 December.

evidence.quote: known as the "Land of Festivals," offers a glimpse into the vibrant and rich Naga heritage
The most prominent among them is the world-famous "Hornbill Festival," held annually from December 1-10.

NGB13.claim: Most visitors pass through Dimapur on the way to Kohima, 75 km away; Chumukedima, 14 km into the hills, was the first headquarters of the Naga Hills district; Dzuleke, two hours away, is good for camping.

evidence.quote: just 75 kilometers away
Situated 14 kilometers into the hills, Chumukedima Village
Dzuleke , approximately a two-hour drive from Dimapur, offers an excellent camping experience

NGB14.claim: October to March is the best time to visit Dimapur, with mild weather of about 15–25°C.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit Dimapur is during the cooler months from October to March.
usually ranging between 15°C and 25°C

NGB15.claim: The Kachari Rajbari ruins in Dimapur are about 100 mushroom-domed sandstone pillars, 8 to 15 feet tall, from the Kachari kingdom.

evidence.quote: Approximately 100 sandstone pillars stand sentinel within this ancient domain in 3 orderly rows.
these monoliths, ranging in height from 8 to 15 feet, proudly exhibit the architectural prowess of the Kacharis.

NGB16.claim: The ruins are open 9 am to 4 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09:00 AM
Closing time - 04:00 PM

NGB17.claim: Dimapur's markets sell woven shawls, bamboo products and tribal jewellery; Hong Kong Market mixes Naga garments and crafts with everyday goods; Ruzaphema Bazaar, 5 km out on the Kohima road, has tribal handicrafts.

evidence.quote: find intricately woven shawls, bamboo products, tribal jewellery
the Hong Kong Market, a melting pot of local and imported goods
About 5 kms from the city centre, on the road to Kohima, is the Ruzaphema Bazaar

NGB18.claim: Listed stays in Dimapur include Jungjung Homestay at Darogapathar and Hesso Villa at Nepali Basti, plus Weaver's Place at Diezephe.

evidence.quote: 55 Jungjung Homestay H.NO 27 Darogapathar, Dimapur
57 Hesso villa homestay Nepali bosti Dimapur
58 Weaver’s Place Diezephe Village

NGB19.claim: The Kohima War Cemetery is open 9 am to 4 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09:00 AM
Closing time - 04:00 PM

NGB20.claim: Beyond the Hornbill Festival, Kohima's year includes the Angami Sekrenyi in February and the Rengma Tseminyu festival in April.

evidence.quote: Witness the Angami tribe's Sekrenyi, a purification ritual seeking good fortune, in February.
Join the joyous celebration of the spring harvest with the Rengma Nagas during their Tseminyu Festival in April.

NGB21.claim: New Market is one of Kohima's oldest, for fruit, vegetables and spices; the Old Market and Tribal Market sell shawls, bags, bamboo baskets and Naga handicrafts.

evidence.quote: New Market is one of Kohima's oldest markets
Journey back through time at the Old Market, where traditional Naga handicrafts meet fashion.
Tribal Market, an unmissable stop for traditional Naga handicrafts

NGB22.claim: Nagaland Tourism lists many Kohima homestays and paying guests, and a cluster at Kipfuzha in Kigwema village near the Naga Heritage Village.

evidence.quote: 1 Pusa Homestay Near VIP Guest House , Minister Hill Kohima
21 South view Homestay Kipfuzha ,KigwemaVillage near Naga Heritage Village
17 Eco stay Hostel TCP Gate Kohima

NGB23.claim: Mokokchung, about 145 km from Kohima, is the homeland of the Ao Naga and known as the 'Land of Pioneers'.

evidence.quote: Situated around 145 km from Kohima, the state’s capital
Renowned as the ‘Land of Pioneers’ for its educational contributions to Nagaland
It is also the homeland of the Ao people, a major Naga tribe.

NGB24.claim: Ungma is the oldest and largest village in the district, and the Ao Moatsu festival takes place in early May.

evidence.quote: Head first to Ungma village, the oldest and largest village in the Mokokchung district.
The three-day Moatsu festival in early May bursts with community spirit

NGB25.claim: October to April is the best time to visit Mokokchung.

evidence.quote: The ideal time to explore Mokokchung is during the post-monsoon or winter season, from October to April.

NGB26.claim: Must-try dishes include bamboo-steamed fish, axone, smoked pork with bamboo shoot, tenga patta and anishi; zutho is the local rice beer.

evidence.quote: Some of the must-try dishes include bamboo steamed fish, axone (fermented soybean), smoked pork with bamboo shoot, tenga patta and anishi.
Zutho is a fermented rice beer

NGB27.claim: Ao artisans make shawls, sling bags, headgear and mekhala, and work in cane and bamboo.

evidence.quote: Their shawls, sling bags, headgear, and wraparound garments (mekhala) are true works of art

NGB28.claim: Marvel Guest House in Mokokchung is on the official list.

evidence.quote: 60 Marvel Guest House Pentacostal Church Alongmen War, Tongdentsuyong Ward Mokokchung

NGB29.claim: Dzükou Valley lies on the Nagaland–Manipur border at about 8,045 ft, and is famous for the Dzükou lily, which blooms in early July.

evidence.quote: Situated between the states of Nagaland and Manipur, this valley is a testament to nature's unparalleled artistry.
At an elevation of 8045 feet
What sets this valley apart is its remarkable transformation in the first weeks of July when it becomes adorned with a vibrant carpet of wildflowers.

NGB30.claim: The trek is about nine kilometres (five to six hours) from the Viswema or Jakhama side; take a local guide.

evidence.quote: The trek spans approximately nine kilometres and can be completed in about five to six hours.
you have the option of two routes: the established Viswema route or the newer, shorter Jakhama route.
it is important to have a local guide with you

NGB31.claim: Kohima's Mary Help of Christians Cathedral, begun in 1986 and consecrated in 1991, covers 25,000 sq ft and seats up to 3,000; the compound holds 20,000.

evidence.quote: The construction of this impressive structure began in 1986, and the church was consecrated in 1991.
The building covers an area of 25,000 square feet
can accommodate up to 3000 people, while the entire compound can hold up to 20,000 people

NGB32.claim: It is open 8 am to 5 pm; prayers are held between 8 am and 4 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 08:00 AM Closing time - 05:00 PM
you can attend the prayers held between 8 AM and 4 PM

NGB33.claim: Diezephe, 13 km from Dimapur, is a community of about 500 artisans and weavers; it won bronze as Best Tourism Village 2023.

evidence.quote: a 500-strong community of skilled artisans and weavers
Located 13 kms from Dimapur
awarded as the bronze recipient, Best Tourism Village 2023

NGB34.claim: Kohima Botanical Garden has medicinal plants, orchids and many bamboos; it is open 9 am to 4 pm.

evidence.quote: from valuable medicinal plants to exquisite orchids and diverse bamboo varieties
Opening time - 09:00 AM Closing time - 04:00 PM

NGB35.claim: Pulie Badze Wildlife Sanctuary near Kohima, set up in 1980, covers about 9.23 sq km with over 250 plant species; open 6 am to 5 pm.

evidence.quote: Spread across approximately 9.23 square kilometres
over 250 unique plant species
Established in 1980
Opening time - 06:00 AM Closing time - 05:00 PM

NGB36.claim: Molungkimong, 39 km from Mokokchung, is believed to date from 1303; the first church in Nagaland was founded there on 22 December 1872.

evidence.quote: Molungkimong village is located 39 kilometres from the Mokokchung district
It is believed that the village has existed since 1303 AD.
This event took place on 22nd December 1872
the first church of Nagaland was established

NGB37.claim: The Naga Heritage Village at Kisama preserves the heritage of Nagaland's ethnic groups with a cluster of 16 morungs, and is the venue of the Hornbill Festival.

evidence.quote: Welcome to the Naga Heritage Village or Kisama Village.
You will be greeted by a cluster of 16 houses, each individually called a "Morung."
The main venue of the Hornbill Festival is held at the Kisama Heritage Village

NGB38.claim: The Government of Nagaland has organised the Hornbill Festival since 2000; it showcases tribal dances, crafts, food, wrestling and traditional games.

evidence.quote: Since the year 2000, the Government of Nagaland has been organising the Renowned Hornbill Festival annually during the first week of December.
Witness the raw power and agility of Naga wrestlers.
Participate in indigenous games like fire-making, archery, and stone-pulling.

itineraries.title: Nagaland in 6 days: Dimapur crafts, Kohima and Ao country at Mokokchung
itineraries.summary: Diezephe's weavers and the Kachari ruins in Dimapur, Kohima's cathedral and green hills, then north to Mokokchung, Ungma and Molungkimong in Ao Naga country.
itineraries.seoDescription: 6 days across Nagaland: Diezephe craft village, Kachari ruins, Kohima's cathedral and sanctuaries, then Mokokchung, Ungma and Molungkimong — with ILP fees and hours.

plan.overview: A slower, culture-led trip that goes beyond Kohima. Start among Dimapur's craftspeople, climb 75 km to Kohima, then head 145 km north to Mokokchung, homeland of the Ao Naga and Nagaland's 'Land of Pioneers'. Every non-indigenous visitor needs a Nagaland ILP.
plan.season: October to April; Ao Moatsu in early May

guides.title: How to reach and get around Nagaland
guides.summary: The Nagaland ILP and its fees, Dimapur airport and railhead, and road distances to Kohima, Kisama, Khonoma, Dzükou and Mokokchung.
guides.seoTitle: How to Reach Nagaland: ILP, Dimapur, Kohima Distances
guides.seoDescription: Getting into Nagaland: the online ILP (₹200 Indians, ₹500 foreigners), Dimapur airport and rail, and distances to Kohima, Kisama, Khonoma, Dzükou and Mokokchung.

body.intro: Every trip to Nagaland starts with a permit and with Dimapur, the state's airport and railhead on the plains. From there the road climbs 75 km to Kohima, the base for most of the sights.

items.title: Who needs one
items.body: Anyone who isn't an indigenous inhabitant of Nagaland, Indian or foreign.

items.title: Fees
items.body: ₹200 per person for Indian tourists and ₹500 for foreign tourists, each valid 30 days.

items.title: How
items.body: Apply online. Tourists need a local contact, not a guarantor; in working hours approval may take about four hours.

items.title: Foreign nationals
items.body: Wikipedia lists the whole of Nagaland as a Protected Area; confirm the current rule before you book.

items.title: Dimapur
items.body: Dimapur Airport and Dimapur railway station are the nearest to Kohima.

items.title: Dzükou trailheads
items.body: Viswema and Jakhama, both within about 25 km; the trek is about 9 km.

checklist: Get your ILP before you travel.
Arrange a local guide for Dzükou.

guides.title: Best time to visit Nagaland: seasons and festivals
guides.summary: October to March for mild weather, December for the Hornbill Festival, and the tribal festivals and Dzükou lily that fill the rest of the year.
guides.seoTitle: Best Time to Visit Nagaland: Hornbill and Festivals
guides.seoDescription: When to visit Nagaland: mild October–March, the Hornbill Festival on 1–10 December, Sekrenyi in February, Moatsu in May and the Dzükou lily in early July.

body.intro: Nagaland calls itself the Land of Festivals, and the best time to go often depends on which one you want to see. The cool, dry months from October suit most travel.

items.title: Hornbill Festival
items.body: 1–10 December at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama; organised by the state since 2000.

sections.heading: Dzükou Valley
sections.text: The Dzükou lily blooms in early July, the valley's most famous sight.
